<description>
This is a low-prio style cleanup for years, but:

* It is tedious and possibly distracting to do it manually when touching the line for other reasons.
* The topic recently came up again when discussing log injection (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35833#issuecomment-5113804332)

So I wonder if a simple scripted-diff can cover the bulk of the changes now, with hopefully little conflicts with reviewed pull requests.

(Removing the trailing newlines from the remaining log messages is trivial and can be done in a later pull)
</description>

nit: I think we can make the concept arg a callable, which would let us inline the strings:

Inline the format strings as callables

```diff
diff --git a/src/test/util_string_tests.cpp b/src/test/util_string_tests.cpp
index 73ee89ce54..17a54e101e 100644
--- a/src/test/util_string_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/test/util_string_tests.cpp
@@ -16,17 +16,12 @@ using util::detail::CheckNumFormatSpecifiers;

 BOOST_AUTO_TEST_SUITE(util_string_tests)

-namespace {
-constexpr char NO_TRAILING_NEWLINE[] = "format string without a trailing newline";
-constexpr char TRAILING_NEWLINE[] = "format string ending in a newline\n";
-
-template <const char* str>
+template <auto str>
 concept IsStrictFormatString =
-    requires { typename std::bool_constant<(ConstevalFormatString</*num_params=*/0, /*permit_trailing_newline=*/false>{str}, true)>; };
+    requires { typename std::bool_constant<(ConstevalFormatString</*num_params=*/0, /*permit_trailing_newline=*/false>{str()}, true)>; };

-static_assert(IsStrictFormatString<NO_TRAILING_NEWLINE>);
-static_assert(!IsStrictFormatString<TRAILING_NEWLINE>);
-} // namespace
+static_assert( IsStrictFormatString<[] { return "format string without a trailing newline"; }>);
+static_assert(!IsStrictFormatString<[] { return "format string ending in a newline\n"; }>);

 template <unsigned NumArgs>
 void TfmFormatZeroes(const std::string& fmt)
```
